d_plane.curve: the spin axis tilts by face - path against spin loft (dynamic loft - attack); face open to the path curves the ball away from the golfer (a fade for a right-hander)
d_plane.source: TrackMan, 'D-Plane' explanations (Jorgensen, The Physics of Golf, 2nd ed. 1999; TrackMan newsletters); shares are typical, varying with loft and strike

launch.form: launch = attack + share x (dynamic loft - attack)
launch.source: TrackMan launch-angle guidance; Penner (2001), 'The physics of golf: the optimum loft of a driver', Am. J. Phys. 69:563-568

face_friction.form: the ball's speed along the face is at most this share of its speed off it: past it the ball slides, as at a wide open lob wedge
face_friction.source: Cross (2002), 'Grip-slip behavior of a bouncing ball', Am. J. Phys. 70:1093-1102; Penner (2003), 'The physics of golf', Rep. Prog. Phys. 66:131-171 (ball on clubface, about 0.4)

spin.form: spin rises with club speed x spin loft, cut by anything between face and ball
spin.source: Penner (2001); Cross & Nathan (2007), 'Performance versus moment of inertia of sporting implements'

partial_swing_speed_share.source: golf instruction 'clock system' wedge data (e.g. Pelz, Short Game Bible, 1999): a 9:00 backswing at about 60-65% of full speed

overswing.source: golf++ design: past full, a little speed for much wider dice
